title: Sharing some progress in my mobile game after 7 months of work to create the hiking management sim I've always wanted. This is just a tiny piece of one tutorial map, but I've become quite proud of my systems of systems that make these little worlds go round. Enjoy! Roast please.
author: idun0

replies.author: idun0
replies.body: thank you! I've spent a long time on it :) changes based on weather, temperature, humidity in the air, time of year, lat/long of the map and looks different in a variety of world scenaiors like fog and mist and rain and more.

replies.author: remorej
replies.body: I especially like how the clouds are light from below, and they appear to have different altitudes. Very nice work. Is that open sourced? I would add some of those to my own night sky.

replies.author: idun0
replies.body:
thank you for noticing lol I didn't think any one ever would. I spent so much time on the under lighting because I think it adds so much! Not open source, custom setup built around Three.js and GLSL shaders, but I’m happy to share a bit about the approach.

The clouds are layers of animated noise, with darker cores and brighter edges to suggest volume without simulating full volumetric clouds. Clouds, rain, and ground shadows share weather data, which helps everything feel connected as storms move through.

For the underlighting we approximate how sunlight travels through more atmosphere near sunset, then use that warmer light to illuminate the cloud undersides. Cloud height value change how the light impacts the cloud over the sampled period. so lower sooner, while high wispy clouds can stay pink longer. Heavy storm clouds get much less of that warm glow.

Different layers drift at different speeds, and weather changes blend gradually. A lot of the work was tuning those interactions until the sky felt right for the game. still work to do tbh, but SO much better from when I started this project.

replies.author: remorej
replies.body: The end result is stunning. I focused more on \[the night side\](https://github.com/jerometremblay/hyperfy#watch-the-world-change-from-day-to-night) of it, but I'll give some love to my clouds soon. :)
